Variants.Content: Orders and Battle Standards: The armies of Westeros possess no magical eyes or ears that can span a battlefield. Dust, sheets of rain, tree lines, and hillsides all swallow commands, leaving battle standards, horns, drums, riders, and house sigils as the only language a commander can rely upon. From high ground, what nobles see is whether formations wheel on command; what foot soldiers see is often simply whether their own house banner still stands. A fallen banner does not necessarily mean the commander is dead, yet it is enough to make an entire wing of an army suspect it has been abandoned. Prudent commanders prepare secondary banners, dispatch riders who know the ground, and use repeatable signals; clever enemies use smoke, false banners, slain couriers, and battlefield rumors to make an undefeated army lose touch with itself first.
